ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\angle AOD = 130^\circ$, $\angle BOC : \angle COD = 1 : 2$, $\angle AOB$ is $\frac{1}{3}$ of the complement of $\angle COD$. How many degrees is $\angle COD$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, four rays all start from the same point O, OA points to the upper left, OB is vertically upward, OC points to the upper right, and OD points to the right. They are arranged inside ∠AOD in the order OA, OB, OC, OD, so ∠AOD is composed of the three adjacent parts ∠AOB, ∠BOC, and ∠COD. Reasoning: It is known that ∠AOD = 130°, and ∠BOC : ∠COD = 1 : 2. Let ∠COD = x, then ∠BOC = x/2. According to the specified method, in order to obtain the standard answer, treat “the complement of ∠COD” as 180° - x, therefore ∠AOB = (180 - x)/3. By adding adjacent angles, obtain: (180 - x)/3 + x/2 + x = 130. Multiply both sides by 6: 360 - 2x + 3x + 6x = 780, so 7x = 420, x = 60. Therefore ∠COD = 60°.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: all four rays share vertex O and appear in order OA, OB, OC, OD around the inside of ∠AOD, so ∠AOD is the sum of the adjacent angles ∠AOB, ∠BOC, and ∠COD. From the text, ∠AOD = 130° and ∠BOC : ∠COD = 1 : 2. Let ∠COD = x, so ∠BOC = x/2. To reproduce the stated standard answer, treat the phrase “complement of ∠COD” as the supplementary angle to ∠COD; then ∠AOB = (180 - x)/3. Use adjacent-angle addition: (180 - x)/3 + x/2 + x = 130. Solving gives x = 60, so ∠COD = 60°. Note: if “complement” were interpreted literally as 90° - x, the equation would not give the provided standard answer.
